definitions.explanation: A situation in which the amount of a product available for sale falls short of demand. Used of individual items on store shelves as well as of a whole market.

examples.japanese: マスクが{品不足|しなぶそく}だ。
{台風|たいふう}の{影響|えいきょう}で{野菜|やさい}が{品不足|しなぶそく}になった。
examples.english: Vegetables ran short because of the typhoon.

examples.japanese: {部品|ぶひん}の{品不足|しなぶそく}が{続|つづ}いており、{新車|しんしゃ}の{納車|のうしゃ}は{半年待|はんとしま}ちだそうだ。
examples.english: The parts shortage is continuing, and delivery of a new car reportedly takes six months.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {品不足|しなぶそく}になる: to run short
- {品不足|しなぶそく}が{続|つづ}く: for a shortage to continue
- {品不足|しなぶそく}が{解消|かいしょう}される: for a shortage to be resolved
- {深刻|しんこく}な{品不足|しなぶそく}: a serious shortage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {品切|しなぎ}れ: sold out — the stock of one item at one shop is gone
- {在庫切|ざいこぎ}れ: out of stock — focuses on the inventory itself
- {供給不足|きょうきゅうぶそく}: supply shortage — more technical, used of markets and industries
